newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 29.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Opposition is building among some of the state attorneys general against a settlement plan with the tobacco industry that would limit future liability.
* The Federal Trade Commission accused R.J. Reynolds Tobacco of seeking to entice youngsters to smoke their Camel cigarettes by using the cartoon character "Joe Camel" in advertisements.
* Intel counter-sued Digital Equipment Corp over a patent infringement dispute, and threatened to cut off its supply of Pentium chips.
* The Nasdaq Stock Market plans to allow all of its stocks to be traded in 1/16-point increments starting on Monday.
* Nearly five dozen metro areas posted unemployment rates below 3 percent in April.
* Orders for durable goods rose 1.4 percent in April.
* LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton plans to buy back Guinness Plc's stake in jointly owned distribution ventures, potentially undermining Guinness' planned merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc.
* Germany's Bundesbank criticized a government plan to revalue the nation's assets to meet standards for participation in the European monetary union.
* Seagram Co Ltd sold more than half of its stake in Time Warner Inc for $1.39 billion to Merrill Lynch & Co.
* The NASD formed a panel to review whether to stop forcing all sex, race and age-discrimination claims into arbitration.
* Novell Inc plans to lay off about 1,000 workers and reduce its inventory.
* Coffee prices soared to a 20-year high, prompting several retailers to announce further price increases.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission is pushing the nation's stock markets to change what it considers to be the "anticompetitive" features of their Intermarket Trading System.

* Heard on the Street: What do you get when you marry one controversial stock with another? More controversy. Wall Street yesterday gave the raspberry to the proposed $10.9 billion megamerger of CUC International and HFS, despite the two companies' contention that CUC's direct-marketing capabilities will help HFS cross-sell services to customers of its real estate, hotel, rental car and vacation timeshare franchises.
* Credit Markets: bonds ended little changed, although prices gyrated through the session in relatively high volume.
